decisions.quote:
For the replication, I accessed the same data source as Kolk (2019). For the WPEI,
the latest version is version 12, and data from different versions is not comparable.
Because the version of data used in the original research was not clearly stated, I tried
several versions of the dataset and contacted the V-Dem Institute to gain access to the
version 7.1 data used in the original study. However, I found it difficult to replicate the
specifications of Kolk’s (2019) sample size exactly. Instead of including data from 1,993
cumulative years, my replication includes 2,054 cumulative years, 61 more years of data
than in the original sample, because after Kolk (2019) published his original paper, the
latest TFR data became available. Kolk did not specify the exact period he used for each
country. I have provided summative statistics regarding the differences between my
replication and Kolk’s (2019) original paper in the Appendix Figure A-4. The difference
between most countries captured by the newest data compared with the data Kolk (2019)
used is just one to two years of data. As I discuss later, additional years would not have
any great impact on Kolk’s (2019) original conclusion except for a small coefficient
fluctuation in the regression.

The main HGEI/tempo analyses also alter measured variables and use1280/649country-year subsets. Accessing the same sources or same countries is not proof of identical original observations. Current source thus combines reconstruction of original analyses with changed historical observations/measurements; the record-level allocation between original-data reproduction and different-sample replication remains genuinely unresolved under the mutually exclusive schema. The author’s reconstruction agreement and sensitivity conclusion remain explicit conditional findings, but cannot unconditionally establish the original-computation recovery axis for a nonidentical panel, or be transferred into a categorical outcome without resolving type. This is an actual data/scope limitation stated in the complete paper, not unavailable local reading or a demand for a particular file format.

previous_decisions.quote: Kolk’s (2019) original analysis was based on Stata software; in this study, I try to replicate Kolk’s (2019) finding in R version 4.1.3. Specifically, I replicate Figures 1, 2, and 3 in Kolk’s original paper. My visualisation is based on the ggplot2 package, version 3.4.0. The result of my replication is shown in the Appendix Table A-1 and Figures A-1 to A-3. For the replication, I accessed the same data source as Kolk (2019). For the WPEI, the latest version is version 12, and data from different versions is not comparable. Because the version of data used in the original research was not clearly stated, I tried several versions of the dataset and contacted the V-Dem Institute to gain access to the version 7.1 data used in the original study.
previous_decisions.reason: Rather than collecting new data in a fresh sample, the study re-analyses Kolk's (2019) historical country-year panel data from the Human Fertility Database and V-Dem version 7.1 in R to verify the original Figures 1-3 and OLS models (Appendix), and then conducts sensitivity/robustness re-analyses on the overlapping 1950-2003 subset of 32 of the 35 original countries by substituting an alternative historical gender equality measure (HGEI) and tempo-adjusted TFR.
